sentences.en: Frivolous, extravagant, libertine, orgiastic, lesbian, incestuous and bloodthirsty.
sentences.zh: 轻浮、奢侈、放荡、荒淫、女同、乱伦且嗜血。

sentences.en: A poisoner and an infanticide.
sentences.zh: 一个下毒犯兼杀婴凶手。

sentences.en: Marie Antoinette tried her hand at every crime.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安托瓦内特尝试过所有的罪行。

sentences.en: Through her wickednesses, she caused the revolution.
sentences.zh: 正是通过她的种种邪恶，她引发了革命。

sentences.en: She ruined the country, brought the people to despair, drove them to revolt.
sentences.zh: 她毁了国家，使人民陷入绝望，逼得他们起义。

sentences.en: All must be revealed.
sentences.zh: 一切都必须被揭露。

sentences.en: It was from your lechery that our gothers were emptied to pay for your pleasures.
sentences.zh: 正是由于你的淫荡，我们的国库才被掏空来支付你的享乐。

sentences.en: So declared the anonymous author of The Cause of the French Revolution or the Secret Conduct of Marie Antoinette of Austria, Queen of France, published in 1790.
sentences.zh: 1790年出版的《法国革命的起因或奥地利的玛丽·安托瓦内特，法国王后的秘密行径》一书的匿名作者如是宣称。

sentences.en: After having brought about the fall of the Ancien Régime, she struggled to preserve it.
sentences.zh: 在导致旧制度灭亡之后，她又竭力维护它。

sentences.en: She was corruption personified, infinitely decadent.
sentences.zh: 她简直是腐败的化身，极端颓废。

sentences.en: So that was Chantal Thomas in La Reine Celerate, The Wicked Queen.
sentences.zh: 那是尚塔尔·托马斯在《绝代艳后》中的观点。

sentences.en: Her biography, her account of Marie Antoinette through the eyes of the propaganda against her, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是她的传记，也是她通过当时的反宣传视角对玛丽·安托瓦内特的解读，汤姆。

sentences.en: And what a way to kick off our great new series on the French Revolution than with libertinism, orgiastic behavior.
sentences.zh: 还有什么比从放荡和荒淫开始更好的方式来开启我们关于法国革命的伟大新系列节目呢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Incest, bloodthirstiness.
sentences.zh: 乱伦，嗜血。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Everything we associate with French history, and the perfect way for us, Tom, and the rest is history, to greet the beginning of the Paris Olympics.
sentences.zh: 所有我们与法国历史联系在一起的东西，汤姆，这也是我们与《历史其余皆传奇》栏目一起迎接巴黎奥运会开幕的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, yeah, the eyes of the world are on Paris and France.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，全世界的目光都聚焦在巴黎和法国。

sentences.en: So how better for us to contribute a series on what is probably, Dominic, I mean, one of the great seismic events, not just in European, but in global history.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，我们制作一个关于这件可以说是欧洲乃至全球历史上最震撼的事件之一的系列节目，还有什么比这更好的方式呢。

sentences.en: Certainly one of the two or three greatest stories in world history.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是世界历史上两三个最伟大的故事之一。

sentences.en: I mean, the rollercoaster of bloodshed, violence, utopianism, insurrection, excitement, you name it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，流血、暴力、乌托邦主义、起义、激情的过山车，应有尽有。

sentences.en: In fact, such a terrific story, Tom, that we're going to take at least two series, probably three series, to do it justice, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一个如此精彩的故事，汤姆，我们要用至少两个系列，很可能是三个系列来讲述它，才能不负它的精彩，对吧？

sentences.en: So this is the kickoff for our first series, which will take us through the first couple of years of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们第一个系列的开篇，它将带我们走过革命最初的几年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we're going to look at some of the causes, some of the background to the revolution,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将探讨革命的一些起因、一些背景，

sentences.en: and then we'll take through the storming of the Bastille and go up to the point where the king, Louis XVI, and his queen, Marie Antoinette, who we've just been hearing about,
sentences.zh: 然后我们将讨论攻占巴士底狱，直至国王路易十六和他的王后玛丽·安托瓦内特——也就是我们刚才听到的这位——

sentences.en: trying to get out of France.
sentences.zh: 试图逃离法国的那一刻。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And spoiler alert, they fail.
sentences.zh: 剧透警告，他们失败了。

sentences.en: And that is the cliffhanger on which we will leave it.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我们将要留下的悬念。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because of course, everybody knows what will then happen to the king and queen.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，每个人都知道接下来这位国王和王后会遭遇什么。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think Marie Antoinette is a kind of wonderful focus for looking at some of the causes.
sentences.zh: 我认为玛丽·安托瓦内特是审视某些起因的一个极好的切入点。

sentences.en: I mean, she's one of the instantly kind of recognisable figures.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她是最让人一眼就能认出的人物之一。

sentences.en: She must be one of the two or three most well-known people in all French history, I would have said.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，她一定整个法国历史上最广为人知的两三个人物之一。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as that kind of bravura passage that you quoted from Chantal Thomas's wonderful book suggests, at the time,
sentences.zh: 正如你引用的尚塔尔·托马斯那本精彩著作中的华彩段落所暗示的那样，在当时，

sentences.en: she is seen by enthusiasts for the revolution as the absolute embodiment of everything that prompted it.
sentences.zh: 革命的热情支持者将她视为促成这一切的绝对化身。

sentences.en: You know, she is kind of the incarnation of ancien régime, arrogance, of aristocratic splendour,
sentences.zh: 你知道，她某种程度上就是旧制度的傲慢、贵族的光辉，

sentences.en: and of a kind of quality of vampirism that has leeched the French people of what should be rightfully theirs.
sentences.zh: 以及一种吸血鬼特质的化身，这种特质抽干了法国人民本应拥有的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, so in her lifetime, before and then particularly after the revolution, she is the object of absolutely kind of obsessive hatred.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以在她生前，在革命前，特别是革命后，她成为了绝对狂热仇恨的目标。

sentences.en: And it's also a kind of prurient hatred, you know, because it is tied up with kind of fantasies about what she's been getting up to.
sentences.zh: 而且这也是一种好色的仇恨，你知道的，因为它与关于她一直在搞什么鬼的幻想交织在一起。

sentences.en: And I guess that, I mean, that runs through to the present day, because the one phrase that everyone would associate with her, let them eat cake, is still repeated, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这，我是说，这一直延续到了今天，因为每个人都会与她联系在一起的那句话，“让他们吃蛋糕吧”，至今仍被反复提起，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that she never said it.
sentences.zh: 尽管事实上她从未说过这句话。

sentences.en: She never said it.
sentences.zh: 她从未说过。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: The original phrase is qu'ils mangent de la brioche.
sentences.zh: 最初的话是：qu'ils mangent de la brioche。

sentences.en: So let them eat brioche has slightly different connotations, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以“让他们吃布里欧修”有着稍微不同的含义，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, because I always kind of imagine, you know, a big gatto with kind of strawberries on the top or something.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我总是会想象，你知道的，一个上面有草莓之类的大蛋糕。

sentences.en: But she never said it anyway, so there's no point in dissecting it, I guess, to some degree, other than the fact that people think she said it.
sentences.zh: 但她反正没说过，所以我觉得在某种程度上没有必要去剖析它，除了人们以为她说过这一点。

sentences.en: Is indicative of this idea of her and Louis, who's supposedly kind of a puppet, them living this life of unbelievable depravity and licentiousness.
sentences.zh: 这表明了她和路易——据说他是个傀儡——过着这种令人难以置信的堕落和放荡生活的观念。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And arrogance and not caring.
sentences.zh: 还有傲慢和漠不关心。

sentences.en: All of which, well, not all of which is completely wrong, but there are definitely huge problems with that.
sentences.zh: 所有这些，好吧，倒也不是完全错误，但这里面绝对存在巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Nuances.
sentences.zh: 微妙之处。

sentences.en: Against that, against the image of Marie Antoinette as a kind of depraved vampire, there's also been, right from the beginning, for conservatives,
sentences.zh: 与此相对，与玛丽·安托瓦内特作为堕落吸血鬼的形象相对的，从一开始，保守派就有一种感觉：

sentences.en: a sense that she is the archetype of the victims of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 她可以说是革命受害者的原型。

sentences.en: Her fate exemplifies what critics of the revolution see as its destructiveness, as its kind of bloodluSt.
sentences.zh: 她的命运体现了革命批评者所看到的毁灭性以及某种嗜血性。

sentences.en: So the revolution itself is cast as a vampire.
sentences.zh: 因此，革命本身就被塑造成了一个吸血鬼。

sentences.en: And in England, the person who classically first articulates that is the Irish politician and Whig, so not even a Tory, Edmund Burke,
sentences.zh: 而在英国，经典地首次表达这一点的是爱尔兰政治家兼辉格党人——甚至都不是托利党人——埃德蒙·伯克，

sentences.en: who November 1790 wrote reflections on the revolution in France.
sentences.zh: 他在1790年11月写下了《法国革命论》。

sentences.en: And in that, he famously recalls seeing Marie Antoinette kind of 16 or 17 years before at the court, glittering like the morning star full of life and splendor and joy.
sentences.zh: 在书中，他深情地回忆起16或17年前在宫廷中看到玛丽·安托瓦内特的情景，她闪耀如晨星，充满生机、光彩和快乐。

sentences.en: And he famously enthuses, I thought 10,000 swords must have leaped from their scabbards to avenge even a look that threatened her with insult.
sentences.zh: 他热情洋溢地宣称：“我曾认为，哪怕只是一个眼神对她构成了侮辱的威胁，也会有成千上万把宝剑出鞘去复仇。”

sentences.en: But the age of chivalry is gone, that of sophistas, economists and calculators has succeeded, and the glory of Europe is extinguished forever.
sentences.zh: 但骑士精神的时代已经过去，诡辩家、经济学家和计算者的时代已经取而代之，欧洲的荣耀永远熄灭了。

sentences.en: Edmund Burke's, I would say, among biographers and among people who studied the revolution, it's his take, actually, that is more enduring than the let them eat cake,
sentences.zh: 埃德蒙·伯克的观点，我想说，在传记作家和研究革命的人当中，实际上比“让他们吃蛋糕”的观点更经久不衰，

sentences.en: she's a vampire school of thought, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 也就是“她属于吸血鬼学派”这一说法，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because actually now, I would say most writers are filled with horror when they look at what happened to Marie Antoinette,
sentences.zh: 因为实际上现在，我想大多数作家在看到玛丽·安托瓦内特遭遇时都充满了惊骇，

sentences.en: this young girl who arrived in France and was turned into a hate figure for the mob.
sentences.zh: 这个年轻的女孩来到法国，却被变成了一个供暴民痛恨的人物。

sentences.en: Chantal Thomas, who we opened with, her book is about the vituperation that is kind of lashed on Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 我们开篇提到的尚塔尔·托马斯，她的书就是关于泼向玛丽·安托瓦内特的辱骂。

sentences.en: And she has a section where she talks about how biographers through the 19th and into the 20th century would debate about whether these were true or not.
sentences.zh: 她有一节讲述了19世纪到20世纪的传记作家们如何争论这些事情是真是假。

sentences.en: And she just says, you know, none of these stories about the incest and the vampirism are true.
sentences.zh: 而她只是说，你知道，所有关于乱伦和吸血鬼的故事都不是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, they're obviously not true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们显然不是真的。

sentences.en: And she says that most recent biographies have been written, to quote her, with sympathy, if not with love.
sentences.zh: 她说，最近的大多数传记都是——引用她的话说——“带着同情，即使不是带着爱”写出来的。

sentences.en: And I would say that's probably true of her as well, because she wrote a novel that then got turned into a film called Farewell, My Queen in English that featured Diane Kruger.
sentences.zh: 我想这在她身上也同样适用，因为她写了一部小说，后来被拍成了英文电影《再见吾王》，由黛安·克鲁格主演。

sentences.en: So Helen of Troy in Troy as Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 就像《特洛伊》里的海伦一样饰演玛丽·安托瓦内特。

sentences.en: And that's a French film.
sentences.zh: 那是一部法国电影。

sentences.en: But of course, Marie Antoinette has also been a kind of an American pinup.
sentences.zh: 但当然，玛丽·安托瓦内特也曾成为某种美国的性感海报女郎。

sentences.en: So a film that was massively popular with my daughters when they were growing up, came out in 2006, is Sophia Coppola's Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 所以有一部在我的女儿们成长过程中极其受欢迎的电影，于2006年上映，那就是索菲亚·科波拉的《绝代艳后》。

sentences.en: Kirsten DunSt.
sentences.zh: 克斯汀·邓斯特主演。

sentences.en: In which she's kind of cast as, you know, very much a contemporary heroine.
sentences.zh: 在片中她被塑造为一个非常现代的女主角。

sentences.en: She's surrounded by her squad.
sentences.zh: 她被她的闺蜜团环绕。

sentences.en: She's got converse trainers in the cabinet.
sentences.zh: 她的鞋柜里有匡威运动鞋。

sentences.en: You know, she rushes around Versailles to new wave bands.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她在凡尔赛宫里伴随着新浪潮乐队的音乐四处奔跑。

sentences.en: And what was interesting about that, I was kind of reading up about the reception of it in France, because it was premiered at Cannes.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我当时读到了一些关于它在法国的反响的报道，因为它是在戛纳首映的。

sentences.en: And there it was greeted with boos and then with cheers.
sentences.zh: 在那里，它迎来了嘘声，然后是欢呼声。

sentences.en: So kind of answering boos and cheers by the French journalists who've been watching it.
sentences.zh: 所以观看它的法国记者们发出了混杂的嘘声和欢呼声。

sentences.en: Which I guess kind of sums up a massive division in France itself.
sentences.zh: 我想这可以说是法国本身巨大分裂的写照。

sentences.en: About her.
sentences.zh: 关于她。

sentences.en: Because Marie Antoinette stands for the revolution to some degree.
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，玛丽·安托瓦内特代表了革命。

sentences.en: Because what you think of Marie Antoinette, you know, you ask an educated Frenchman or Frenchman what they think of Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 因为你对玛丽·安托瓦内特的看法，你知道的，你问一个受过教育的法国人或法国女性他们对玛丽·安托瓦内特的看法。

sentences.en: And their answer will tell you what they think of the revolution, probably.
sentences.zh: 他们的回答大概会告诉你他们对革命的看法。

sentences.en: And probably also where they stand politically even today in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 而且可能也说明了他们在21世纪的今天在政治上的立场。

sentences.en: Don't you think?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I do.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我确实这么认为。

sentences.en: And I think to a degree that may be true as well in the broader world, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在某种程度上，在更广阔的世界里或许也是如此。

sentences.en: But I mean, it's much more focused in France, obviously.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，很明显它在法国更加集中。

sentences.en: And I think that that sense of ambivalence, you know, is Marie Antoinette a monster or is she a victim?
sentences.zh: 我认为这种矛盾的情感，你知道的，玛丽·安托瓦内特是个怪物还是个受害者？

sentences.en: Is she someone to be detested and loathed?
sentences.zh: 她是一个应该被痛恨和厌恶的人吗？

sentences.en: Or is she someone to be pitied and admired?
sentences.zh: 还是一个应该被同情和赞赏的人？

sentences.en: That's an ambivalence that is there even before the revolution.
sentences.zh: 这种矛盾心理在革命之前就已经存在了。

sentences.en: So the way that she is viewed by the French public is a kind of mixture of loathing and desire.
sentences.zh: 因此，法国公众看待她的方式是厌恶与渴望的某种混合体。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because she's not always hated.
sentences.zh: 因为她并不总是招人恨。

sentences.en: That's an important point to make.
sentences.zh: 这是需要指出重要一点。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, she's very popular with certain segments of society.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她在社会的某些阶层中非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And I think that she's cast either as a kind of emblem of royal grace, because, as we will see, in a way, she's a very, very modern figure.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为她要么被塑造成皇室优雅的象征，因为正如我们将看到的，在某种程度上，她是一个非常非常现代的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: She kind of basically, I think, invents the French ideal of fashion.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她基本上开创了法国的时尚理想。

sentences.en: She's way ahead of the game.
sentences.zh: 她远远走在了时代的前面。

sentences.en: But to other people, this makes her the kind of the embodiment of frivolity or decadence.
sentences.zh: 但对其他人来说，这使她成为了轻浮或颓废的化身。

sentences.en: And she's a very proactive queen.
sentences.zh: 而且她是一个非常积极主动的王后。

sentences.en: Queens in France generally are not expected to play a proactive role in court life, still less national life.
sentences.zh: 法国的王后们通常不被期望在宫廷生活中扮演积极主动的角色，在国家生活中更是如此。

sentences.en: Marie Antoinette comes to do that.
sentences.zh: 而玛丽·安托瓦内特却这样做了。

sentences.en: And she's a kind of emblem of all the paradoxes that we'll be talking about in the context of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 她可以说是我们在革命背景下将要讨论的所有悖论的象征。

sentences.en: And the fact that she's a figure of fantasy is really crucial, because not just her, but the revolution itself is about the creation of stories,
sentences.zh: 而且她是一个充满幻想的人物，这真的很关键，因为不仅是她，革命本身也关乎故事的创造，

sentences.en: the projection of stories and narratives onto facts of the economy, agriculture, the crowds, the court, everything.
sentences.zh: 将故事和叙事投射到经济、农业、民众、宫廷以及一切事实之上。

sentences.en: It's how you structure the story that basically determines your attitudes to the revolution, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，正是你构建故事的方式基本上决定了你对革命的态度。

sentences.en: Totally agree, Tom.
sentences.zh: 完全同意，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, historians like Simon Sharma and Robert Danton have written brilliant books about how the French Revolution is a sort of hall of mirrors or hall of narratives, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，像西蒙·沙玛和罗伯特·达顿这样的历史学家写过精彩的书籍，讲述法国革命是如何成为一种镜厅或叙事之厅的，我想是的。

sentences.en: Very appropriate for Versailles, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常适合凡尔赛宫，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So let's start not at Versailles, but with Marie Antoinette herself.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们不要从凡尔赛宫开始，而是从玛丽·安托瓦内特本人开始。

sentences.en: So she is born, Tom, in 1755.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，她出生于1755年。

sentences.en: And of course, the single most important thing about her, I would say, is that she is not French.
sentences.zh: 当然，关于她最重要的一点，我想说的是，她不是法国人。

sentences.en: She is Austrian.
sentences.zh: 她是奥地利人。

sentences.en: She is.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: We love the Habsburgs on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我们在《历史其余皆传奇》里都很喜欢哈布斯堡王朝。

sentences.en: I don't think there'll ever be a historical podcast in the history of mankind that is so keen on the Habsburgs, as the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我想人类历史上绝不会再有第二个历史播客像《历史其余皆传奇》这样对哈布斯堡王朝如此热衷了。

sentences.en: We've had Edward Habsburg talking about the Habsburgs.
sentences.zh: 我们请过爱德华·哈布斯堡谈论哈布斯堡家族。

sentences.en: We've had Franz Ferdinand, a great friend of the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我们请过弗朗茨·斐迪南，《历史其余皆传奇》的好朋友。

sentences.en: And now another Habsburg, Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 现在又是另一个哈布斯堡家族成员，玛丽·安托瓦内特。

sentences.en: Yes, although she's born, Maria Antonia.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管她出生时的名字叫玛丽亚·安东尼娅。

sentences.en: And I think that it's fair to say that her identity as an Austrian and as a Habsburg is kind of fundamental, both to how her admirers see her and how her detractors see her.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为公平地说，她作为奥地利人和哈布斯堡家族成员的身份，对于她的崇拜者和批评者如何看待她都是至关重要的。

sentences.en: So to her admirers, she is an embodiment of a new age of peace between what traditionally have been the great rivals in European politics.
sentences.zh: 因此，在她的崇拜者看来，她是欧洲政治中传统大敌之间迎来和平新时代的化身。

sentences.en: So going right the way back to the 16th century, Charles V and François I, these are the people who are kind of tearing Europe up while Luther is busy getting on with his stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以一直追溯到16世纪，查理五世和弗朗索瓦一世，当路德正忙于他自己的事情时，正是这些人把欧洲撕裂了。

sentences.en: And France and the Habsburg Empire have been the great geopolitical rivals on the continent of Europe.
sentences.zh: 法国和哈布斯堡帝国一直是欧洲大陆上的两大主要地缘政治对手。

sentences.en: But this has changed over the course of the 18th century due to the emergence of two new great powers.
sentences.zh: 但由于两个新兴大国的出现，这种情况在18世纪发生了变化。

sentences.en: One of those is Britain, very happy to say.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是英国，我很高兴这么说。

sentences.en: So in the Seven Years' War, Britain is taking on France and winning as a kind of global power.
sentences.zh: 所以在七年战争中，英国作为全球强权正在与法国对抗并取得胜利。

sentences.en: But on the continent, there's the emergence of Prussia.
sentences.zh: 但在欧洲大陆上，普鲁士崛起了。

sentences.en: And Prussia is hungry for a lot of Austria's traditional territories.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士对奥地利的许多传统领土虎视眈眈。

sentences.en: And under its great king, Frederick II, it annexes a province called Silesia, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 在其伟大的国王腓特烈二世的领导下，它吞并了一个叫做西里西亚的省份，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which is basically now, it's a chunk of Poland.
sentences.zh: 基本上现在它是一大块波兰领土。

sentences.en: And the Habsburgs are terribly upset about this.
sentences.zh: 哈布斯堡家族对此感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And basically, they kind of enter into an alliance with France so that they can get Silesia back.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们与法国结盟，以便夺回西里西亚。

sentences.en: And France enters into an alliance with Austria so that she can have a counterweight to Britain.
sentences.zh: 因此，法国与奥地利结盟，以便拥有一个抗衡英国的力量。

sentences.en: So the diplomatic revolution, historians call this, because it's such a seismic moment in European history.
sentences.zh: 因此，历史学家称之为“外交革命”，因为这是欧洲历史上一个极其重大的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the Seven Years' War breaks out in 1756 with Britain and Prussia against Austria and France.
sentences.zh: 于是，七年战争于1756年爆发，英国和普鲁士对抗奥地利和法国。

sentences.en: And the following year, a very heavyweight figure in French politics, the Duc de Choiseul, arrives in Vienna as the French ambassador.
sentences.zh: 第二年，法国政坛一位极具分量的人物——舒瓦瑟尔公爵——作为法国大使抵达维也纳。

sentences.en: And the rulers who greet him, they're a couple, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 迎接他的统治者是一对夫妇，对吧？

sentences.en: So the emperor is Francis I.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的皇帝是弗朗茨一世。

sentences.en: But the person who's really kind of cracking the whip is his wife, the empress, Maria Theresa.
sentences.zh: 但真正掌权发号施令的是他的妻子，女皇玛丽亚·特蕾西亚。

sentences.en: And she is a very, very proficient politician.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非常非常出色的政治家。

sentences.en: Indeed, one might say stateswoman.
sentences.zh: 确切地说，可以说是女政治家。

sentences.en: But she's also very, very fertile.
sentences.zh: 但她也非常非常能生。

sentences.en: And the Habsburgs have always, I mean, it's been their boast, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且哈布斯堡家族一直以来——我的意思是，这一直是他们的傲人之处，对吧？

sentences.en: That some empires get their way by fighting.
sentences.zh: 有些帝国靠打仗来达到目的。

sentences.en: We do it by marrying off our children.
sentences.zh: 而我们则是通过把孩子们嫁出去来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And Maria Antonia is their 11th daughter, and as it will turn out, their last daughter.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·安东尼娅是他们的第11个女儿，事实证明，这也是他们的最后一个女儿。

sentences.en: And the reason that the Duc de Choiseul is interested in her is that she is one year younger than the grandson of Louis XV, the French king, also inevitably called Louis.
sentences.zh: 舒瓦瑟尔公爵对她感兴趣的原因是，她比法国国王路易十五的孙子小一岁，这个孙子也无可避免地叫路易。

sentences.en: And his very fertile mind is thinking, well, you know, we could maybe marry them off.
sentences.zh: 他那活跃的脑筋便盘算着，嗯，你知道的，我们或许可以让他们联姻。

sentences.en: A brilliant way to cement the alliance and to ensure that the alliance endures.
sentences.zh: 这是巩固同盟并确保同盟持久的绝妙方法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so in due course, Choiseul goes back from Vienna.
sentences.zh: 因此，在适当时机，舒瓦瑟尔从维也纳返回。

sentences.en: He goes back to Paris and he becomes the foreign minister.
sentences.zh: 他回到巴黎，并成为了外交大臣。

sentences.en: Basically the kind of almost the prime minister for Louis XV.
sentences.zh: 基本上就相当于路易十五的首相。

sentences.en: And he's kind of pushing this idea.
sentences.zh: 他一直在推行这个想法。

sentences.en: He's saying we should really try and cement this alliance.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们真的应该努力巩固这个同盟。

sentences.en: And it comes into further focus in 1765 when Louis XV's son, and therefore the father of this Louis who is being lined up to marry Maria Antonia, he dies.
sentences.zh: 1765年，路易十五的儿子——也就是即将与玛丽亚·安东尼娅联姻的那位路易的父亲——去世了，这让事情变得更加明确。

sentences.en: And so the grandson of Louis XV is now the Dauphin, the kind of French equivalent to the Prince of Wales, the heir to the throne.
sentences.zh: 因此，路易十五的孙子现在成了王储，也就是法国相当于威尔士亲王的储君。

sentences.en: And he's 11 and Maria Antonia is then 10.
sentences.zh: 当时他11岁，玛丽亚·安东尼娅10岁。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And on the 4th of April, 1770, it's all agreed.
sentences.zh: 1770年4月4日，一切都敲定了。

sentences.en: The marriage contract is signed.
sentences.zh: 婚约正式签署。

sentences.en: There's a kind of weird thing where they do a proxy marriage in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 还有一件挺奇特的事，他们在维也纳举行了一场代办婚礼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So the new emperor, Maria Theresa's son, Joseph, he stands in for the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 所以新皇帝、玛丽亚·特蕾西亚的儿子约瑟夫代替了王储。

sentences.en: And then two days later, Maria Antonia is put into a carriage, along with 56 other carriages.
sentences.zh: 两天后，玛丽亚·安东尼娅坐上一辆马车，随行的还有另外56辆马车。

sentences.en: And they set off from Vienna to go to France.
sentences.zh: 他们从维也纳出发前往法国。

sentences.en: And people who are enthusiasts for this alliance think this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 那些热衷于这个同盟的人认为这简直妙极了。

sentences.en: Absolutely wonderful.
sentences.zh: 绝对棒极了。

sentences.en: But of course, in France, there are lots of people who are not enthusiasts.
sentences.zh: 但当然，在法国，也有很多人并不热心。

sentences.en: Because as you said, I mean, these are ancestral enemies.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，我的意思是，这些都是世仇。

sentences.en: They have, of course, come together under the pressure of Prussia and Britain.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们在普鲁士和英国的压力下走到了一起。

sentences.en: But culturally and imaginatively, the idea of Austria to most French men and women is as this horrendous place.
sentences.zh: 但在文化和想象中，对大多数法国男人和女人来说，奥地利是个极其可怕的地方。

sentences.en: Our enemies, the Austrians can't be trusted.
sentences.zh: 我们的敌人，奥地利人是信不过的。

sentences.en: And that baggage, she is never able to shed it for the rest of her life.
sentences.zh: 这种历史包袱，她一生都无法摆脱。

sentences.en: So right the way through her career and to an escalating degree, she is always referred to as le trichienne, so the Austrian.
sentences.zh: 所以在她整个生涯中，而且程度愈演愈烈，人们总是称她为le trichienne，也就是“奥地利女人”。

sentences.en: But if you put the emphasis on chienne, that's bitch in France.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把重音放在chienne上，在法国这就成了“贱货”。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So it's the kind of the ostrich bitch.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像“奥地利贱货”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So she's always being portrayed either as an ostrich or as a dog.
sentences.zh: 因此，她总是被描绘成一只鸵鸟或是一条狗。

sentences.en: Or both.
sentences.zh: 或者两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: And the weird thing is, is that this isn't actually remotely fair, because her father is basically French.
sentences.zh: 诡异的是，这其实一点也不公平，因为她的父亲基本上是法国人。

sentences.en: So Francis I, you know, he's the Duke of Lorraine.
sentences.zh: 所以弗朗茨一世，你知道的，他是洛林公爵。

sentences.en: He is of French royal descent.
sentences.zh: 他拥有法国王室血统。

sentences.en: And there's a case for saying that Marie Antoinette is actually one of the most French queens that the Bourbon, the royal dynasty, have ever had.
sentences.zh: 有理由认为，玛丽亚·安托瓦内特实际上是波旁王朝历代王后中最具法国血统的一位。

sentences.en: Because normally they're marrying foreign queens who have no French connections at all.
sentences.zh: 因为通常他们迎娶的外国王后与法国毫无渊源。

sentences.en: But what's interesting is that, you know, her father basically gets written out of the story.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，你知道的，她的父亲基本上被从这个故事里抹去了。

sentences.en: And she is portrayed as being her mother's daughter, solely her mother's daughter.
sentences.zh: 而她被描绘成她母亲的女儿，纯粹只是她母亲的女儿。

sentences.en: Maria Theresa is seen as this terrifying virago who is out to destroy France.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·特蕾西亚被视为一个可怕的悍妇，一心想要毁掉法国。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: She's had a French tutor called the Abbe de Vermont, who turns up and is appalled to discover that Marie Antoinette, basically she hasn't had any education at all.
sentences.zh: 她曾有一位名叫德韦蒙特修道院长的法国家庭教师，他来后震惊地发现玛丽亚·安托瓦内特基本上根本没受过什么教育。

sentences.en: And throughout her life, she has no interest in books.
sentences.zh: 而且她一生对书本毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: She's not remotely intellectual.
sentences.zh: 她一点也不知识分子。

sentences.en: Although she is interested in kind of the cultural temperature, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 尽管她对某种文化风向很感兴趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, she is.
sentences.zh: 对，她是的。

sentences.en: But it's said of her that no one has ever seen her finish a book.
sentences.zh: 但关于她，人们常说从没见过她读完一本书。

sentences.en: And I think that that is kind of widely believed.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种看法相当普遍。

sentences.en: And he complains of a quality that will be repeatedly applied to her, which is her légèreté, her frivolity, her lightness.
sentences.zh: 而且他抱怨了她身上一个会被反复提及的特质，那就是她的轻浮、轻率，她的浅薄。

sentences.en: The fact that she is not a heavy person.
sentences.zh: 她不是一个沉稳的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think it would be fair to say.
sentences.zh: 这样说应该挺公道的。

sentences.en: But he also acknowledges that, you know, she has great charm.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也承认，你知道的，她非常有魅力。

sentences.en: She has great poise.
sentences.zh: 她仪态万千。

sentences.en: She is also not conventionally pretty because she has, you know, the classic protuberant lower lip of a Habsburg.
sentences.zh: 她长得也不是传统意义上的漂亮，因为她有着哈布斯堡家族经典的突出的下唇。

sentences.en: But she, you know, she has, the Abbe says, a perfect porcelain complexion.
sentences.zh: 但修道院院长说，她拥有完美的瓷器般的肤色。

sentences.en: She has brilliant blue eyes.
sentences.zh: 她有着明亮的蓝眼睛。

sentences.en: She has a very sweet oval face.
sentences.zh: 她有一张非常甜美的鹅蛋脸。

sentences.en: So basically, you know, she will do.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你知道的，她还算过得去。

sentences.en: Robert Danson in his book, The Revolutionary Temper, says that when the pamphleteers, newspapers and whatnot, were talking about her in France,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·丹顿在他的书《革命气质》中提到，当法国的小册子作家、报刊等等谈论她时，

sentences.en: they all said she's actually very nice looking.
sentences.zh: 他们都说她其实长得非常好看。

sentences.en: You know, she's blonde hair, beautiful pale complexion.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她金发碧眼，肤色白皙动人。

sentences.en: She looks like a queen.
sentences.zh: 她看起来就像个女王。

sentences.en: She does.
sentences.zh: 她的确如此。

sentences.en: And as we will see, she becomes a great icon of beauty and fashion and style.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，她成为了美丽、时尚和风格的伟大偶像。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of symbolic moment where she ceases to be Austrian and becomes French, which is, you know, she's traveling up from Vienna with her 57 carriages.
sentences.zh: 有一个象征性的时刻，标志着她不再是奥地利人，而是成为了法国人，也就是，你知道的，她坐着57辆马车从维也纳一路北上。

sentences.en: And on the 7th of May, 1770, they reach the Rhine and there's an island in the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 在1770年5月7日，他们抵达莱茵河，河中央有一座岛屿。

sentences.en: And this wooden pavilion has been built that looks like a kind of, you know, perfectly tiny chateau.
sentences.zh: 那里建起了一座木制亭子，看起来像是一个非常精致的小城堡。

sentences.en: And it has five rooms inside it.
sentences.zh: 里面有五个房间。

sentences.en: And there's kind of two on the Austrian side, two on the French side.
sentences.zh: 奥地利一侧有两个房间，法国一侧有两个房间。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of room in the middle.
sentences.zh: 中间还有一个房间。

sentences.en: And Marie Antoinette goes into the Austrian rooMs.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·安托瓦内特进入了奥地利房间。

sentences.en: She's divested of her clothes down to her kind of underwear.
sentences.zh: 她被脱去衣物，只剩下贴身的内衣裤。

sentences.en: She's then put into a French ceremonial dress.
sentences.zh: 然后她换上了法国的礼服。

sentences.en: She's led into the central drawing room.
sentences.zh: 她被带进了中央的客厅。

sentences.en: The door leading into the French rooms is opened.
sentences.zh: 通往法国房间的门打开了。

sentences.en: She looks back.
sentences.zh: 她回过头去。

sentences.en: The Austrian doors have been shut.
sentences.zh: 奥地利那边的门已经关上了。

sentences.en: All the Austrian servants have vanished.
sentences.zh: 所有的奥地利随从都消失了。

sentences.en: And Marie Antoinette is handed over to this terrifying woman who is the maîtresse d'etiquette,
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·安托瓦内特被交给了这个可怕的女人，她就是宫廷礼仪女官长，

sentences.en: the woman who is going to instruct her in the ritual of the court called the Comtesse de Neuil.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个将要向她传授宫廷繁文缛节的诺伊尔伯爵夫人。

sentences.en: What was that noise?
sentences.zh: 刚才那是什么声音？

sentences.en: Comtesse de Neuil.
sentences.zh: 诺伊尔伯爵夫人。

sentences.en: Neuil.
sentences.zh: 诺伊尔。

sentences.en: Neuil.
sentences.zh: 诺伊尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's just too many vowels.
sentences.zh: 对，元音实在太多了。

sentences.en: There's basically four vowels in that.
sentences.zh: 那里面基本上有四个元音。

sentences.en: Neuil.
sentences.zh: 诺伊尔。

sentences.en: Scrabble heaven.
sentences.zh: 拼字游戏的天堂。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 对，确实是。

sentences.en: And Marie Antoinette bursts into tears at the side of this terrifying woman, flings herself into the Comtesse's arMs.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·安托瓦内特一看到这个可怕的女人就放声大哭，扑进了伯爵夫人的怀里。

sentences.en: The Comtes, massively embarrassed, very stiff, shrugs her off, performs a low curtsy.
sentences.zh: 伯爵夫人极其尴尬，身体僵硬，把她推开，行了个低身礼。

sentences.en: Marie Antoinette apologises and says, pardon me, these are for the family and the fatherland I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 玛丽亚·安托瓦内特道歉说，请原谅我，这些眼泪是为我所离开的家族和祖国而流的。

sentences.en: For the future, I shall not forget that I am French.
sentences.zh: 今后，我不会忘记我是法国人。

sentences.en: And the Comtesse de Neuil says, yeah, you better not.
sentences.zh: 诺伊尔伯爵夫人说，最好是这样。

sentences.en: I'm here to whip you into shape.
sentences.zh: 我来这儿就是为了调教你的。

sentences.en: So off they go.
sentences.zh: 于是他们出发了。

sentences.en: And Tom, just one thing.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，还有一件事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 什么。

sentences.en: She is 14 years old.
sentences.zh: 她才14岁。

sentences.en: She's not yet 15.
sentences.zh: 还不到15岁。

sentences.en: Imagine what an unbelievably terrifying moment this must be for her.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，对她来说，这该是多么难以置信的可怕时刻。

sentences.en: And what makes it even worse, she has an adorable little dog who she has to leave behind.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，她有一只可爱的小狗，却不得不把它留在身后。

sentences.en: But we'll come to that later.
sentences.zh: 但我们稍后再谈这个。

sentences.en: It's a crucial part of the story.

sentences.zh: 所以她非常像一个名人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And there's a quality of the fact that I think she's very impressed by the sense she has of her own virtue.
sentences.zh: 而且其中有一种特质是，我认为她对自身美德的意识感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: And she wants people to know about it while simultaneously genuinely being worried about it.
sentences.zh: 她既想让别人知道这一点，同时又确实发自内心地对此感到担忧。

sentences.en: I mean, all of those things can be true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些事情是可以同时成立的。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And she wants to make sure that her children are raised in this.
sentences.zh: 她希望确保自己的孩子也能在这种环境中长大。

sentences.en: She's a very, very good mother, a very attentive mother.
sentences.zh: 她是一个非常好、非常细心的母亲。

sentences.en: So 1784, the year before that, it had been a terrible winter.
sentences.zh: 所以在1784年，也就是前一年，那是一个可怕的冬天。

sentences.en: And she provides her children with what one of her companions describes as a lesson in doing good by bringing in a great kind of pile of toys and then saying,
sentences.zh: 她给孩子们上了一课，用她的一位同伴的话来说，就是“行善的一课”，她搬来了一大堆玩具，然后说：

sentences.en: you can't have these because we're going to sell these toys and use them to get blankets and bread among children in need.
sentences.zh: “你们不能要这些，因为我们要把这些玩具卖掉，用卖得的钱为贫困儿童购置毛毯和面包。”

sentences.en: Oh, that's quite surprising.
sentences.zh: 哦，这挺让人意外的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Very celebrity on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 非常有推特上名人的做派。

sentences.en: That's why it's a Keynesian, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，这就是凯恩斯主义的体现。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's very Dickensian.
sentences.zh: 这非常狄更斯。

sentences.en: That as well.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So Chantal Thomas describes this wonderfully.
sentences.zh: 尚塔尔·托马斯对此有精妙的描述。

sentences.en: She was fond of charity and never tired of the spectacle of her own goodness.
sentences.zh: 她热衷慈善，且永远看不够自己善良的宏大场面。

sentences.en: So I think, again, she is a precursor of a kind of modern type of celebrity there.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，从某种意义上说，她也是现代名人类型的一大先驱。

sentences.en: Kind of celebrity charity.
sentences.zh: 某种名人慈善。

sentences.en: The Duchess of Sussex, Tom.
sentences.zh: 苏塞克斯公爵夫人，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A slight quality there.
sentences.zh: 有点那个意思。

sentences.en: So that's on the kind of the moral level.
sentences.zh: 所以这是在道德层面上的。

sentences.en: But she also creates this kind of new kind of fashion that is absolutely repudiating the kind of the stiff formality of Versailles.
sentences.zh: 但她还开创了一种全新的时尚，彻底摒弃了凡尔赛宫那种死板的繁文缛节。

sentences.en: So she has this dressmaker, Rose Bertin, who shockingly is allowed ready access to her apartments.
sentences.zh: 她有一位女裁缝叫罗丝·贝尔坦，令人震惊的是，她被破例允许随时出入她的公寓。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, she doesn't go through all the court protocols that normally restricts people who can see the queen.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她不用经历那些通常限制面见女王人数的宫廷礼节。

sentences.en: And basically, Marie Antoinette is kind of discarding all the rich silks of the court for flowing white muslins,
sentences.zh: 基本上，玛丽·安托瓦内特抛弃了宫廷里所有华丽的丝绸，换上了飘逸的白色细棉布，

sentences.en: for kind of simple costumes, fresh flowers, kind of bucolic adornments.
sentences.zh: 换成了那种简单的服饰、新鲜的花朵和类似田园风光的装扮。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And not only that, she stops wearing corsets and stays and all those things that kind of really button you up.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，她不再穿紧身胸衣、排骨撑以及所有那些把你勒得紧紧的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Again, it's very Russo.
sentences.zh: 这又非常卢梭。

sentences.en: Go back to nature.
sentences.zh: 回归自然。

sentences.en: It's going back to nature.
sentences.zh: 这就是回归自然。

sentences.en: I mean, Sharma says you can actually see what her body looks like under the dress,
sentences.zh: 我是说，夏尔马说过，你实际上能看出她裙子底下的身体轮廓，

sentences.en: which, of course, is not the case with the incredibly rigid and structured dresses that people are wearing.
sentences.zh: 这当然是那些极度僵硬且结构复杂的宫廷礼服所不具备的。

sentences.en: It's not that they're wearing them earlier.
sentences.zh: 并不是说她们之前就穿。

sentences.en: They're wearing them at the same time.
sentences.zh: 她们是同时代在穿。

sentences.en: But she is breaking with the rules a French kind of hierarchical dress.
sentences.zh: 但她打破了法国阶级化着装的规则。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I said that Marie Antoinette, in a way, invents modern fashion.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我刚才说玛丽·安托瓦内特在某种程度上发明了现代时尚。

sentences.en: And she does that because she is, whatever the French say, she is the queen of France.
sentences.zh: 她之所以能做到这一点，是因为不管法国人怎么说，她都是法国王后。

sentences.en: For that reason, she has the highest profile of any woman in Europe.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，她是欧洲所有女性中知名度最高的一个。

sentences.en: But also because she's a genius at it.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为她在这方面是个天才。

sentences.en: And the idea of waking up every morning and just deciding what you want to wear, you know, what clothes you're going to have,
sentences.zh: 每天早晨醒来，就决定自己想穿什么，你知道的，决定穿什么衣服，

sentences.en: how you're going to do your hair, rather than having it prescribed according to rigid structures, is something revolutionary, you know, literally revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 决定如何做发型，而不是按照死板的体制来规定，这种想法是革命性的，字面意义上的革命性。

sentences.en: Because this is the style of fashion that will come in during the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是法国大革命期间将会兴起的时尚风格。

sentences.en: And Marie Antoinette, to that extent, I think is the godmother of France's modern reputation as the home of fashion.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上讲，我认为玛丽·安托瓦内特是法国作为时尚之都的现代声誉的教母。

sentences.en: And we've talked about clothes.
sentences.zh: 我们已经聊过衣服了。

sentences.en: There is also hair.
sentences.zh: 还有发型。

sentences.en: So there's an absolutely wonderful book with the great title Marie Antoinette's Head by Will Bashaw,
sentences.zh: 有一本非常精彩的书，书名很棒，叫《玛丽·安托瓦内特的头发》，作者是威尔·巴肖，

sentences.en: which is about her hairdresser, who is a man called Monsieur Léonard, who will feature throughout the story.
sentences.zh: 讲的是她的发型师，一个叫莱昂纳尔先生的男人，他将在整个故事中出场。

sentences.en: And again, this is very, very shocking that he's a male hairdresser.
sentences.zh: 同样，一个男发型师这非常非常令人震惊。

sentences.en: You know, not a lady's maid.
sentences.zh: 要知道，不是女仆。

sentences.en: He's a celebrity hairdresser.
sentences.zh: 他是名人发型师。

sentences.en: And like Madame Bertin, has ready access to her.
sentences.zh: 就像贝尔坦夫人一样，可以随时面见她。

sentences.en: So there's something very, very diva about this.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有歌剧名伶的架势。

sentences.en: I mean, it's absolutely recognisable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对让人一眼就能认出来。

sentences.en: And he gives her a whole succession of kind of unbelievably grandiose hairstyles.
sentences.zh: 他为她设计了一连串不可思议的宏伟发型。

sentences.en: So the hairstyle that Marie Antoinette is initially promoting is called Le Pouf Sentimental.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽·安托瓦内特最初推广的发型叫做“情感蓬蓬头”（Le Pouf Sentimental）。

sentences.en: The sentimental pouf.
sentences.zh: 情感蓬蓬头。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a hard sentence to carry off, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难驾驭对吧？

sentences.en: You can imagine they're kind of teased up gores and plumes and things.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象那些高高梳起的衬垫、羽毛之类的东西。

sentences.en: Very, very risky because, you know, there are candles in the chandeliers.
sentences.zh: 非常非常冒险，因为你知道的，枝形吊灯上有蜡烛。

sentences.en: So if you brush against it, it might just go up in flames.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你擦过它，它可能就会直接着火。

sentences.en: And there are various kind of styles.
sentences.zh: 而且有各种各样的款式。

sentences.en: So you have the hérisson, which is unpowdered hair.
sentences.zh: 比如刺猬头（hérisson），也就是不扑粉的头发。

sentences.en: So that's kind of going back to nature there.
sentences.zh: 这有点回归自然的意思了。

sentences.en: And they're kind of curled to the tips and rising in tears.
sentences.zh: 它们的发梢卷曲，层层叠叠向上耸立。

sentences.en: So it looks like an hérisson, a hedgehog.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来像一只刺猬（hérisson）。

sentences.en: There's the zephyr, which is flowers woven into the hair.
sentences.zh: 还有西风头（zephyr），就是将花朵编织进头发里。

sentences.en: So again, there's the sense that you're moving from kind of stiff formality to nature.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，有一种从死板的繁文缛节走向自然的转变感。

sentences.en: And then in 1781, Monsieur Léonard is summoned by Marie Antoinette, who's distraught because she feels that she's losing her hair.
sentences.zh: 然后在1781年，莱昂纳尔先生被玛丽·安托瓦内特召见，她当时心烦意乱，因为她觉得自己正在脱发。

sentences.en: You know, her hair is thinning and Monsieur Léonard is devastated by this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她的头发在变少，莱昂纳尔先生对此感到痛心疾首。

sentences.en: And he goes away and he thinks about it.
sentences.zh: 他走开了，开始思考。

sentences.en: And then he comes back and he does something revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 然后他回来了，做了一件革命性的事。

sentences.en: He cuts her hair.
sentences.zh: 他剪短了她的头发。

sentences.en: He gives her the kaffur à l'enfant, a child's hairstyle.
sentences.zh: 他给她剪了个儿童发型（kaffur à l'enfant）。

sentences.en: He starts to decorate it only with flowers, not with jewels.
sentences.zh: 他开始只用花朵装饰头发，而不用珠宝。

sentences.en: And it creates this fashion for natural hairstyles that spreads across Versailles, spreads across Paris, spreads across France, spreads across Europe.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一种自然发型的时尚，风靡凡尔赛，风靡巴黎，风靡全法国，风靡全欧洲。

sentences.en: And she has people who are around her, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 她身边有一群伙伴，对吧？

sentences.en: She has, you use the expression, her squad, which makes it sound like Taylor Swift.
sentences.zh: 她有，你用了这个词，她的“小分队”，这听起来像是泰勒·斯威夫特。

sentences.en: But she does have this coterie of very, very close friends who will later become,
sentences.zh: 但她确实有这样一个小圈子，由非常非常亲密的朋友组成，她们后来变得

sentences.en: like her, controversial, some of whom, frankly, are doomed to incredibly tragic and blood-curdling ends.
sentences.zh: 和她一样充满争议，其中有些人坦率地说，注定要迎来极其悲惨和毛骨悚然的结局。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there are two in particular.
sentences.zh: 这里面特别有两个人。

sentences.en: There's the Duchesse de Polignac, who, I mean, it's very, very beautiful, exquisite manners, absolutely adores kind of gossip and intrigue.
sentences.zh: 一个是波利尼亚克公爵夫人，我的意思是，她非常非常美丽，举止优雅至极，极度热爱八卦和阴谋。

sentences.en: So I think it's kind of less Taylor Swift.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这不太像泰勒·斯威夫特。

sentences.en: It's more the plastics in Mean Girls, which I know you haven't seen, but which I, as a parent of two daughters, have seen a lot.
sentences.zh: 更像是《贱女孩》里的塑料姐妹花，我知道你没看过，但我作为两个女儿的父亲，看了很多遍。

sentences.en: A brilliant, brilliant film.
sentences.zh: 一部非常非常棒的电影。

sentences.en: And I think that anyone who's seen that film, if you think of Marie Antoinette and the Duchesse de Polignac as the plastics, who are the kind of the queen bees in a high school.
sentences.zh: 我想任何看过那部电影的人，如果把玛丽·安托瓦内特和波利尼亚克公爵夫人想象成“塑料姐妹花”，也就是高中里的那些核心风云人物。

sentences.en: And then there's this sidekick who's always trying to make fetch happen, the word fetch, and she never does.
sentences.zh: 然后还有这个死党，总是试图把“fetch”（酷）这个词流行起来，但她从来没成功过。

sentences.en: And I think that that character would be the Princesse de Lambal, who is very, very vapid.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那个角色就是朗巴勒亲王妃，她非常非常空虚。

sentences.en: There's a kind of brilliantly bitchy account of her by the Comtesse de Gemli.
sentences.zh: 热姆利伯爵夫人对她有过一段精彩且刻薄的描述。

sentences.en: She never had an opinion of her own.
sentences.zh: 她从来没有过自己的观点。

sentences.en: In conversation, she always adopted the opinion of the person who passed for the wittiest in a way that was utterly unique.
sentences.zh: 在谈话中，她总是采纳那些被认为最机智的人的观点，方式极其独特。

sentences.en: Whenever there was a serious discussion, she never spoke, pretending to fall into a trance.
sentences.zh: 每当有严肃的讨论，她从不发言，假装陷入出神状态。

sentences.en: Then she would suddenly appear to snap out of her reverie and repeat word for word, as though it came from her,
sentences.zh: 然后她会突然看起来从冥想中惊醒，并且一字不差地重复

sentences.en: what the person whose opinion she had decided to adopt had just said.
sentences.zh: 刚刚被她决定采纳观点的那个人所说的话，就好像那是她自己说的一样。

sentences.en: She effected great surprise when told someone had just said the same thing.
sentences.zh: 当别人告诉她有人刚刚说过同样的话时，她会表现出极大的惊讶。

sentences.en: She assured everyone she hadn't heard of it.
sentences.zh: 她向所有人保证她没听说过。

sentences.en: So I think you get there a sense that Marie Antoinette likes these people precisely because they are not witty.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得你可以从中感受到，玛丽·安托瓦内特喜欢这些人，正是因为她们不机智。

sentences.en: They are not brilliant.
sentences.zh: 她们并不才华横溢。

sentences.en: She can enjoy their company.
sentences.zh: 她可以享受与她们的陪伴。

sentences.en: Inevitably, gossip will say that they're all lesbians, that they're all engaging in sapphic rights.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，八卦会说她们都是女同性恋，说她们都在进行萨福式的仪式。

sentences.en: The Duchess de Polignac in particular, who becomes widely, widely hated, but both of them are strongly disliked.
sentences.zh: 特别是波利尼亚克公爵夫人，她后来变得极其极其讨人厌，不过她们两个人都非常不受欢迎。

sentences.en: There are also male guests going to the Petit Trianon, of whom the most notorious is a dashing Swedish officer called Axel von Fersen, who is the son of a field marshal
sentences.zh: 还有一些男宾客去小特里亚农宫，其中最臭名昭著的是一位风度翩翩的瑞典军官阿克塞尔·冯·菲尔森，他是某位陆军元帅的儿子，

sentences.en: and who had met Marie Antoinette at a masked ball at the opera in 1774 when she was still the Dauphine, and he hadn't recognised her,
sentences.zh: 1774年在歌剧院的化装舞会上遇到了玛丽·安托瓦内特，当时她还是王太子妃，而他当时没认出她来，

sentences.en: which is obviously a kind of great thrill for Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 这显然对玛丽·安托瓦内特来说是一种巨大的刺激。

sentences.en: And from that point on, the regular visits, the two indisputably become close.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，定期拜访开始了，两人毫无疑问地变得亲密起来。

sentences.en: Again, it is taken for granted that they are sleeping.
sentences.zh: 同样的，外界理所当然地认为他们睡过了。

sentences.en: I think this is most unlikely.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这极不可能。

sentences.en: Because it's not really in her character, you think, yeah.
sentences.zh: 因为这不太符合她的性格，你懂的，对吧。

sentences.en: It's not her style.
sentences.zh: 这不是她的作风。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it would be mad for her to do that.
sentences.zh: 而且她要是那样做就太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But there is clearly a kind of heedlessness about this.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，对此有一种漫不经心的态度。

sentences.en: I mean, to have these kind of very close, intimate relationships and to kind of thumb her nose at the formalities and the hierarchies of Versailles,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，拥有这种非常亲密的关系，却对凡尔赛的礼节和阶级不屑一顾，

sentences.en: to bring down everything that the Comtesse de Nuit had represented.
sentences.zh: 打倒诺阿耶伯爵夫人所代表的一切。

sentences.en: I mean, she's building up trouble for herself.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她是在给自己惹麻烦。

sentences.en: She is.
sentences.zh: 她确实是。

sentences.en: There's an amazing quotation, actually, from her brother, Joseph II, who wrote to their brother, Leopold.
sentences.zh: 其实有一段她哥哥约瑟夫二世的惊人引言，他写信给他们的兄弟利奥波德。

sentences.en: And he said, She has no etiquette.
sentences.zh: 他说，她没有礼节。

sentences.en: She goes out and runs around alone or with a few people without the outward signs of her position.
sentences.zh: 她外出独自闲逛，或只跟几个人一起，没有她身份的外部标志。

sentences.en: She looks a little improper.
sentences.zh: 她看起来有点不得体。

sentences.en: And while this would be all right for a private person, she is not doing her job.
sentences.zh: 虽然这对于平民来说无可厚非，但她没有做好自己的工作。

sentences.en: And that is the issue, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里，不是吗？

sentences.en: That she's not playing the part of a French queen as the French people expect.
sentences.zh: 她没有扮演好法国人民所期望的那种法国王后的角色。

sentences.en: No, she's not.
sentences.zh: 不，她没有。

sentences.en: And I think what is more and even more damaging for her is that she's actually playing the part of a mistress.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为更糟糕、对她打击更大的是，她实际上在扮演情妇的角色。

sentences.en: Because the Petit Trianon is where the mistress lives and queens are not supposed to live like mistresses.
sentences.zh: 因为小特里亚农宫是情妇住的地方，王后本不该像情妇那样生活。

sentences.en: So over the course of Louis XVI's reign going into the 1780s, she's coming to be hated as queens often are hated, as kind of the embodiment of royal arrogance
sentences.zh: 所以在路易十六统治进入1780年代的过程中，她开始遭到痛恨，正如王后们常遭痛恨的那样，作为皇室傲慢

sentences.en: and of kind of absolutism.
sentences.zh: 和专制主义的化身。

sentences.en: But she's also being hated as favourites are.
sentences.zh: 但她也像受宠的情人那样遭到痛恨。

sentences.en: She's being cast as a kind of a voracious, greedy, blood-sucking nymphomaniac.
sentences.zh: 她被塑造成了一种贪婪、嗜血、性欲亢奋的形象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the pair of these images are kind of being fused because a mistress is always being accused of extravagance.
sentences.zh: 这两种形象正在融合，因为情妇总是被指责奢侈挥霍。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Comes with a territory, right?
sentences.zh: 这是职责所在，对吧？

sentences.en: That's what they're there to do.
sentences.zh: 她们存在就是为了干这个。

sentences.en: And kind of amazingly, stories start to be repeated that Marie Antoinette is literally maintaining at the expense of the state a whole tank full of leeches,
sentences.zh: 而且不可思议的是，开始流传这样一种说法：玛丽·安托瓦内特竟然用国家的钱养了一整缸水蛭，

sentences.en: which is a kind of horrible idea.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个可怕的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: A sort of metaphor, yeah.
sentences.zh: 某种隐喻，对吧。

sentences.en: And also, of course, mistresses are sexually promiscuous.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，情妇在性方面都是放荡的。

sentences.en: And so this is why the stories that she's having, you know, sapphic affairs and sleeping with, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么那些关于她有萨福式恋情、与

sentences.en: Swedish officers and things like that, it's why they have such currency.
sentences.zh: 瑞典军官上床之类的事，会流传得如此广泛的原因。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing about that, Tom, is that they start, I think it's Robert Dantamase's point, that they start in 1774, so 15 years before the revolution,
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有趣的是，汤姆，罗贝尔·达恩通的观点是，这些故事始于1774年，也就是大革命爆发前15年，

sentences.en: and when she's still only 18, 19 years old.
sentences.zh: 而当时她才18、19岁。

sentences.en: So very early on, these stories that she has this kind of voracious sexual appetite, that her Locke-obsessed husband is not satisfying, and that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以在很早的时候，这些关于她有着贪婪的性欲、她那个患有包茎的丈夫无法满足她、以及你知道的，

sentences.en: there's this kind of extravagance and depravity, sucking the energy and the money out of France.
sentences.zh: 存在这种奢侈和堕落、在吸干法国的精力和金钱的故事，

sentences.en: They start very early, don't they?
sentences.zh: 就开始得很早，不是吗？

sentences.en: And she's never able to shake them.
sentences.zh: 而且她永远无法摆脱这些传言。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And to reiterate, because I think this is so important, these stories are not coming from Republican people who hate the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 重申一下，因为我觉得这太重要了，这些故事并不是来自痛恨君主制的共和派人士。

sentences.en: It's coming from her rivals at the court.
sentences.zh: 是来自她在宫廷里的竞争对手。

sentences.en: These are the people who are spreading it.
sentences.zh: 正是这些人四处散布的。

sentences.en: And it reflects a character of libertinism that you get at the court, that Louis XV had exemplified, and which you get in Le Clos' great novel,
sentences.zh: 它反映了你在宫廷里能见到的那种放荡不羁的风气，路易十五曾是这种风气的典范，你在拉克洛的小说中也能看到，

sentences.en: Dangerous Liaisons, as it's translated, people who've seen the film.
sentences.zh: 也就是被翻译为《危险关系》的那本书，看过电影的人都知道。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole thing is about debauching people, the idea that the aristocracy are cruel and sexually predatory.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整本书讲的就是腐蚀他人，认为贵族是残忍且在性方面具有掠夺性的。

sentences.en: And of course, the writer who absolutely exemplifies this is the Marquis de Sade, who we did an episode on.
sentences.zh: 当然，绝对能体现这一点的作家是萨德侯爵，我们曾为他做过一期节目。

sentences.en: And there's a sense in which the Marquis de Sade is reworking ideas that are very, very current in pornography at the time.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，萨德侯爵是在重新加工当时色情文学中非常非常流行的思想。

sentences.en: And Marie Antoinette, who had refused to speak to Madame du Barry because she'd been a courtesan, who had been so unsexually voracious
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安托瓦内特曾因杜巴利夫人出身交际花而拒绝与她说话，而这位王后却有着极强的性欲

sentences.en: that the marriage hadn't been consummated for seven years, she comes to be the kind of the protagonist of pornographic fantasies that are increasingly revolting and shocking
sentences.zh: 以至于他们的婚姻七年都没有圆房，她成了色情幻想的主角，这些幻想越来越令人作呕和震惊

sentences.en: in the way that the Marquis de Sade's writings are revolting and shocking.
sentences.zh: 就像萨德侯爵的著作那样令人作呕和震惊。

sentences.en: And listeners may be wondering, well, does any of this matter?
sentences.zh: 听众们可能会想，这有什么大不了的呢？

sentences.en: And it does matter because it comes to threaten the reputation, not just of the queen, but of the king and of the monarchy itself.
sentences.zh: 这确实很重要，因为它开始威胁到不仅是王后，还有国王以及整个君主制的声誉。

sentences.en: The thing is that in the early 1780s, all these rumours and stories and fantasies, they lack an obvious focus.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，在18世纪80年代初，所有这些谣言、故事和幻想都缺乏一个明确的焦点。

sentences.en: They are underground.
sentences.zh: 它们处于地下状态。

sentences.en: They are being percolated by kind of court rivalries.
sentences.zh: 它们正在各种宫廷权力斗争中酝酿。

sentences.en: But then in 1784, there's an absolute catastrophe because Marie Antoinette finds herself engulfed in a complete firestorm of scandal.
sentences.zh: 但到了1784年，发生了一场绝对的灾难，因为玛丽·安托瓦内特发现自己陷入了一场彻底的丑闻风暴中。

sentences.en: And actually, Dominic, it's not just a scandal, it's an affair.
sentences.zh: 说实话，多米尼克，这不仅仅是一场丑闻，这是一桩事件。

sentences.en: The affair of the diamond necklace.
sentences.zh: 钻石项链事件。

sentences.en: It's an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个惊人的故事。

sentences.en: It is an absolutely incredible story.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个令人难以置信的故事。

sentences.en: And you'll be taking us through this tomorrow, actually, won't you?
sentences.zh: 事实上，明天你将带我们了解这件事，对吧？

sentences.en: People don't have to wait.
sentences.zh: 大家不必等待。

sentences.zh: 明天，因为我们将在接下来的两周里持续播出这个系列。

sentences.zh: 现在，如果你想听关于钻石项链事件的内容，然后我们将进入三级会议的召集、巴士底狱的陷落，

sentences.zh: 革命的进程、革命背后的思想，以及国王和王后日益增长的恐慌与恐怖，以及他们逃离法国的决定，
